chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Founding the big band: Century Room, Bales's money, Tomino
summary: Dexter urged him to keep the small band, but he took a Century Room job and enlarged it with Nat Towles men; Bales funded that, and the records paid for the rest.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But Jay, when you started this band, you backed it. I mean, did you have enough money saved or did the Tominos -- I mean, you had to have money for uniforms and all. How did you do that?
But you're skipping something there, Stanley, because you haven't found out how come he let this small band go yet, you know? Jump from one to the other.

Okay, we'll start right there. Well, here's what happened with the small band. Dave Dexter begged me, he says, "Don't ever change this small band. Keep it like it is and let is stay right on through. Don't enlarge. Don't get no big band. Let everything stay like it is."
So I wanted to, but I also wanted to hear a big band. So when the job came along for the big band, I took the job. So I had to get more musicians.
That was at the Century Room and we started to work in the Century Room. So I had to have a bigger band at the Century Room and when I went up to Omaha and got Some
In fact, Mr. Bales gave me the money to do that, to go get these guys. But all other monies come right out of the band. A lot of people they think that Tomino didn't spend no money for that band.
That was all. All that money, everything, from the time we made 'Confessing the Blues,' that was the money that carried the band. That was the money.
It carried itself and a lot of people -- I've heard a lot of people say that the Tominos were spending money on the band but no, that was their own. That band carried itself.
